slides.title: Office politics, *Mahabharata style*
slides.sub: Three people from one dice game still sit in your office. You met them this week.

slides.title: One game. *Three types.*
slides.body: In the Mahabharata, Yudhishthira is invited to a game of dice. He loses everything. Three people made it happen. Swipe to meet them.

slides.title: Shakuni: *"Just one more round"*
slides.body: He played with loaded dice and kept pushing. At work: the one who rushes you into a deal you can't win. Try it: ask "What do I lose?" first.

slides.title: Dhritarashtra: *the boss who won't see*
slides.body: The king knew his son was cheating and let it go. At work: the manager whose favourite gets away with it. Try it: write down your work, with dates.

slides.title: Bhishma: *the senior who stays quiet*
slides.body: The wisest man in the hall knew it was wrong. He didn't stop it. At work: the senior who just nods. Try it: speak up once, calmly.

slides.deva: न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा न ते वृद्धा ये न वदन्ति धर्मम् ।
slides.iast: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā, na te vṛddhā ye na vadanti dharmam
slides.meaning: It is not a real meeting if no wise elders are in it. And they are not real elders if they don't speak up for what is right. (First half of the verse.)
slides.ref: Mahabharata 5.35.49, Vidura Niti (BORI critical ed.); Kumbhakonam ed. 2.89.65

slides.title: Office politics needs *your yes*
slides.body: Yudhishthira knew the game was rigged and still sat down: "Once called, I never turn back." Screenshot this: Ask first. Write it down. Speak up.

slides.title: Send this to *your office group*
slides.sub: Save it for your next tough meeting, and share it with the work friend who has met all three. Follow @sutraverselife for real-life lessons from ancient wisdom.
